questions.stem: The Sun contains 99.8% of the total mass of the Solar System. What is the main consequence of this for the other objects in the Solar System?

options.text: The Sun's light illuminates all the planets equally
The Sun's enormous gravitational pull keeps all the planets, dwarf planets, and other objects in orbit
The Sun's magnetic field prevents the planets from spinning
The Sun's heat keeps all the planets at the same temperature

questions.explanation: The Sun's massive gravitational field (due to its enormous mass) provides the centripetal force that holds all objects in the Solar System in their orbits. Without the Sun's gravity, planets would fly off in straight lines. The Sun does not illuminate planets equally (A) -- intensity decreases with distance. The planets do spin (C). Planets have very different temperatures depending on distance from the Sun (D).

questions.stem: The inner planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars) are rocky, while the outer planets (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune) are gas giants. Which statement best explains this difference?

options.text: The outer planets are newer and have not yet solidified
Close to the young Sun, it was too hot for gases to condense, so only rocky materials could form planets; further out, gases could accumulate
The outer planets captured gas from passing comets
The inner planets lost their gas atmospheres due to collisions with asteroids

questions.explanation: During the formation of the Solar System, the region close to the Sun was too hot for volatile gases (like hydrogen and helium) to condense. Only rocky and metallic materials could survive, forming the smaller terrestrial planets. Further from the Sun, temperatures were low enough for gases to accumulate, forming the much larger gas giants. All planets formed at roughly the same time (A is wrong).

questions.stem: Light from the Sun takes approximately 8 minutes to reach Earth (1 AU away). Approximately how long would light take to reach Jupiter, which is about 5 AU from the Sun?

options.text: 8 minutes
13 minutes
40 minutes
400 minutes

questions.explanation: If light takes 8 minutes to travel 1 AU, then it takes 8 x 5 = 40 minutes to travel 5 AU to Jupiter. Light travels at a constant speed (3 x 10^8 m/s), so the time is directly proportional to the distance. This illustrates the vast scale of the Solar System. Option B adds 5 to 8 rather than multiplying. Option D multiplies 8 x 50 instead of 8 x 5.

questions.stem: A comet has a highly elliptical orbit around the Sun. At which point in its orbit does the comet travel fastest?

options.text: When it is furthest from the Sun
When it is closest to the Sun
Its speed is constant throughout its orbit
When it is at the midpoint between closest and furthest

questions.explanation: A comet travels fastest when it is closest to the Sun (perihelion) because the Sun's gravitational pull is strongest there, accelerating the comet. As the comet moves away from the Sun, gravitational attraction slows it down, so it travels slowest at its furthest point (aphelion). The speed is not constant (C) -- that only applies to perfectly circular orbits.

questions.stem: The correct order of the planets from the Sun outward is:

options.text: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, Uranus, Neptune
Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune
Mercury, Venus, Mars, Earth, Jupiter, Saturn, Neptune, Uranus
Venus, Mercury, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune

questions.explanation: The correct order from the Sun is: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune. Option A swaps Jupiter and Saturn. Option C swaps Mars and Earth, and swaps Neptune and Uranus. Option D swaps Mercury and Venus. A useful mnemonic is 'My Very Educated Mother Just Served Us Nachos.'
